title: Functions
bridge: C functions declare a return type and parameter types: `int clamp(int v, int lo, int hi)`. Parameters are always **copies** (C has no references; pointers do that job, next units). A function must be declared before it's used, often with a prototype at the top or in a `.h` file.

exercises.title: Clamp
exercises.prompt: Write int clamp(int v, int lo, int hi): v, but kept between lo and hi.
hints: Two checks, then the normal case.
if (v < lo) return lo; if (v > hi) return hi; return v;

exercises.title: Factorial (recursion)
exercises.prompt: Write long factorial(int n) using recursion: factorial(5) is 120, and factorial(0) is 1.

tests.why: Call factorial on a smaller problem: factorial(n - 1)

choices: The function's first line with ; so it can be used before it's written

quiz.why: Always copies; pass a pointer to let a function change something.

choices: calls itself until the program crashes (stack overflow)
quiz.why: Every call uses memory until it runs out.

cards.a: A stopping case and a smaller call.

explain: Explain functions to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
